true_answer: Inverse functions only exist for bijections, but f − 1 ( y ) is defined for any function f . The point: f − 1 ( y ) is a set , not an element of the domain. This is just sloppy notation for f − 1 ({ y }) . To help make this distinction, we would call f − 1 ( y ) the complete inverse image of y under f . It is not the image of y under f − 1 (since the function f − 1 might not exist).
